name: Realized return (one period)
formula: \begin{aligned} R_{t+1} &= \dfrac{P_{t+1} + \mathit{Div}_{t+1} - P_t}{P_t} \\[8pt] &= \underbrace{\dfrac{P_{t+1} - P_t}{P_t}}_{\text{capital gain rate}} + \underbrace{\dfrac{\mathit{Div}_{t+1}}{P_t}}_{\text{dividend yield}} \end{aligned}
use: Return of a stock or bond held between two dates.

vars.meaning: realized return between date t and t + 1

pitfall: Bond: use the coupon in EUR, not the coupon rate.
example:
Task type: start price, end price and dividend are given – find the return over the holding period.
Buy at P_t = 50, sell at P_{t+1} = 54, dividend 1 → R = (54 + 1 − 50) / 50 = 10%
= capital gain 8% + dividend yield 2%
Bond bought at 980, coupon 50 EUR, worth 1,000 a year later → (1,000 + 50 − 980) / 980 = 7.14%

name: Return with a stock split
use: Whenever a split or reverse split happens during the holding period.

vars.meaning: number of shares held before the split
number of shares held after the split
share price at the start (before the split)
share price at the end (after the split)
total dividends received on all shares held

pitfall: Never compare one share's price before and after the split – compare the whole position.
example:
Task type: a split happens while you hold the stock – compare the whole position, not one share.
100 shares at 60 = 6,000; 2-for-1 split → 200 shares, end price 33, dividends 100 EUR in total
R = (200 × 33 + 100 − 6,000) / 6,000 = 700 / 6,000 = 11.7%
Wrong: (33 − 60) / 60 = −45%

name: Return over several periods
use: Total return over several years, or with dividends reinvested at each dividend date.

vars.meaning: total (cumulative) return from period 1 to N

example:
Task type: returns for several years (or between dividend dates) are given – find the total return.
+10%, −5%, +20% → 1.10 × 0.95 × 1.20 − 1 = 25.4%
not 10 − 5 + 20 = 25%

name: Arithmetic average
use: Estimate of the expected return of one future period.
pitfall: Not the realized performance per year.
example:
Task type: past annual returns are given – estimate next year's expected return.
+10%, −5%, +20% → R̄ = (10% − 5% + 20%) / 3 = 8.33%

name: Geometric average (CAGR)
use: What an investment actually earned per year in the past.
example:
Task type: past annual returns are given – what did the investment really earn per year?
+10%, −5%, +20% → (1.10 × 0.95 × 1.20)^(1/3) − 1 = 1.254^(1/3) − 1 = 7.84% p.a.
Lower than the arithmetic average of 8.33%.

name: Annualizing a sub-period return
use: Return measured over h years (e.g. h = 0.5 for six months).

vars.meaning: return over the whole holding period
length of the period in years

example:
Task type: a return is given for a period that is not one year – convert it to “per year” so it can be compared.
Stock goes from 100 to 110 in 6 months → R_h = 10%, h = 0.5
R_annual = 1.10^(1/0.5) − 1 = 1.10² − 1 = 21% p.a. (not 2 × 10% = 20%)
+33.1% over 3 years → h = 3 → 1.331^(1/3) − 1 = 10% p.a.

name: Variance and volatility (historical)
use: Risk of one asset from past returns.
pitfall: Divide by T − 1 for historical data; use decimals (0.25² = 0.0625) consistently.
example:
Task type: a series of past returns is given – find the risk of the asset.
+10%, −5%, +20%, R̄ = 8.33% → deviations 0.0167, −0.1333, 0.1167
Var = (0.0167² + 0.1333² + 0.1167²) / (3 − 1) = 0.0317 / 2 = 0.0158 → σ = 12.6%
σ_monthly = 4% → σ_annual = 4% × √12 = 13.9%
